How to start over
in a new city
Walk your new neighbourhood every day for a week. Find your café, your gym, your grocery store. Familiar places make a city feel like home faster.
Join one activity in the first month. A running club, a language exchange, a climbing gym. Regular activities are the easiest way to meet people.
Say yes to every invitation at the start. Colleagues, neighbours, friends of friends. You can be selective later, once you know people.
Learn the history of the city. Its old streets, its famous people, its strange stories. Knowing where you live makes you love it more.
Explore with curiosity. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it helped me discover my new city in a much deeper way.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It helped me discover my new city in a much deeper way.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep in touch with home. A weekly call to family and old friends keeps you grounded while you build something new. Home is still home.
Give it six months. The first weeks can feel lonely. Most people say it takes about half a year before a new city truly feels like home.
